questions.question: Which one sentence best captures the whole portfolio?

answerOptions.text: A repeatable reproduce-and-measure engine run on several recent papers — each an honest, pre-registered, judge-free measurement, with nulls reported as headlines
answerOptions.rationale: It names the engine (repeatability), the discipline (pre-registered, judge-free), and the honesty (nulls as headlines).

answerOptions.text: Six unrelated experiments showing that small models are bad at various tasks
answerOptions.rationale: The through-line is one repeatable engine, not six one-offs, and the point is honest measurement, not 'small models are bad.'

answerOptions.text: A benchmark suite proving frontier models beat cheap ones
answerOptions.rationale: Scope is mechanical reliability of small models under a budget, not a frontier-vs-cheap benchmark.

answerOptions.text: A set of reproductions that all confirm their source papers
answerOptions.rationale: Two projects headline nulls; the work reports honest deltas, not uniform confirmations.

questions.hint: Engine, discipline, honesty — in one breath.

questions.question: 'Lead with the caveat' — which project's headline caveat is 'the gap is injected'?

answerOptions.text: forge-gap
answerOptions.rationale: forge-gap seeds a disclosed transient fault to create the recovery scenario; the injection is its load-bearing caveat.

answerOptions.text: dim-stage
answerOptions.rationale: dim-stage's headline caveat is a pre-registered null and the band-transplant risk, not an injected gap.

answerOptions.text: decay-pin
answerOptions.rationale: decay-pin's caveat is claiming the gap's structure (not the point estimate) and the summarize tail risk.

answerOptions.text: lossy-wall
answerOptions.rationale: lossy-wall's caveat is the matched-budget design and the qwen model substitution.

questions.hint: Which project runs a controlled fault-recovery testbed?

questions.question: Two gaps: A has a Newcombe interval of [+17.3, +48.0]; B has one of [−0.022, +0.103]. Which counts as a reproduced effect?

answerOptions.text: A only — its interval is entirely above zero; B straddles zero and is reported as a null
answerOptions.rationale: Entirely-above-zero is a real effect (forge-gap); straddling zero is a null (ghost-patch).

answerOptions.text: Both, because both point estimates are positive
answerOptions.rationale: A positive point estimate with an interval covering zero is a null, not an effect.

answerOptions.text: B only, because its interval is narrower
answerOptions.rationale: Narrowness is precision, not effect; B still includes zero.

answerOptions.text: Neither, because Newcombe cannot decide effects
answerOptions.rationale: Newcombe is exactly the tool that decides this, via whether the interval excludes zero.

questions.question: Asked 'which is your best work and why?', what is the strongest answer?

answerOptions.text: dim-stage — the deepest project, with a bitwise-validated instrument (AGREE gate) and a pre-registered null answered on the paper's own open question about small models
answerOptions.rationale: It is the highest-status surface: a validated instrument makes the null about the models, and it answers an open question.

answerOptions.text: Whichever had the biggest headline number
answerOptions.rationale: Impressiveness of a number is not the bar; depth and defensibility are, and dim-stage's headline is a null.

answerOptions.text: blind-cite, because it is the newest
answerOptions.rationale: blind-cite is an in-progress M0 pilot — the honest lead is dim-stage, not the newest.

answerOptions.text: forge-gap, because its gap is the largest
answerOptions.rationale: forge-gap's headline gap is injected; leading with it as 'best' invites the manufactured-gap probe.

questions.hint: Deepest, validated instrument, answers an open question.

questions.question: A skeptic says: 'You did not really write this — Claude Code did.' What is the best response?

answerOptions.text: Whether a human or an agent typed a line is not something a skeptic can tell; what they can tell is whether you can reconstruct the reasoning and re-derive every number — which you can
answerOptions.rationale: The portfolio's own principle: optimize for reconstruction, not recall; ownership is understanding, not authorship of keystrokes.

answerOptions.text: 'I wrote every line myself without any tools.'
answerOptions.rationale: Dishonest and beside the point; the credibility is in reconstruction, not in denying tool use.

answerOptions.text: 'It does not matter how it was built.'
answerOptions.rationale: It dodges the probe; the right answer engages it by demonstrating understanding.

answerOptions.text: 'The LLM judge verified the code, so it is correct.'
answerOptions.rationale: There is no LLM judge, and code-correctness is not the same as your understanding.

questions.question: Why is the honesty described as 'load-bearing' rather than a disclaimer?

answerOptions.text: It removes the three ways reproductions cheat — self-graded homework, moving goalposts, hiding misses — which is what turns 'I reproduced it' into a checkable claim
answerOptions.rationale: Each honesty commitment closes a specific credibility hole; together they are the credibility, not an add-on.

answerOptions.text: It makes the write-ups sound more modest
answerOptions.rationale: It is not about tone; it is about structurally removing ways to cheat.

answerOptions.text: It is required by the journals the work is submitted to
answerOptions.rationale: This is hobby-scale open work; the honesty is a design choice, not a submission requirement.

answerOptions.text: It lets the projects avoid reporting nulls
answerOptions.rationale: The opposite — the honesty is why nulls are reported as headlines.
